Class ConnectionHandshaker

java.lang.Object
network.server.core.ConnectionHandshaker
All Implemented Interfaces:
Runnable
public class ConnectionHandshaker extends Object implements Runnable
Performs the handshake for a single socket connection, on the per-connection thread spawned by the ServerMain acceptor (never on the acceptor thread, so a slow or hostile client only stalls itself). All blocking socket I/O lives here: opening the streams, reading the ConnectMessage and writing rejections.

Flow

  1. create the streams and read a ConnectMessage (blocking, timeout 50000 ms);
  2. enqueue the registration on the LobbyManager (submitSocketRegistration) and block on the future with a timeout, receiving only a boolean verdict;
  3. ACCEPT → return: the view/handler and the reader thread have already been built and started by the lobby-thread; REJECT (name taken) → rewrite the error on the same stream and read another ConnectMessage (the socket stays open for the retry); timeout/error → write the error and close.

  • Method Details

    • run

      public void run()
      Runs the name-negotiation loop: read a ConnectMessage, submit the registration and block on the verdict, looping on rejection until a name is accepted or the connection times out / fails. On any unrecoverable I/O or deserialization error the socket is closed and the thread ends.
      Specified by:
      run in interface Runnable

    • sendHandshakeError

      private void sendHandshakeError(ObjectOutputStream out, String message) throws IOException
      Writes an ErrorMessage directly through the handshake's output stream. Used to reject a name attempt without spinning up a full session.
      Parameters:
      out - the handshake output stream
      message - the error text to send
      Throws:
      IOException - if the write fails
